We have not had a chance to get to the beach since it arrive, and the weather is cool enough, it’ll be awhile. But we’re planning our spring outings and this step in wet bag is now on the Take List. Renegade GK Fury Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 6-11, 7 Styles, Level 4) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 4+3MM Giga Grip | High Performance Pro-Level Goalkeeper Glove | Based in The USA This is an absolutely fantastic keeper glove with just one nuance with the right thumb fingersave.

The gloves are nice and cool with a mesh that lets the hand breathe on the back. The grip is great even though it is smooth! The palms are solid and feel like a mix of latex and neoprene and seem to breathe so my palms don't get as sweaty as other gloves. The latex is a bit soft and after a half-dozen practices with 4-5x the shots I would have in a game, it hasn't disappointed. However, there are some chunks that are missing. I change gloves nearly every season or two. There is a latex wraparound for the thumb that keeps the grip throughout the throw to my teammates. It's like I am getting an extra yard or two and can put a little spin on the ball if I like.

The hard ball comes in up high like a hornet and it's easy to swat down. I just don't feel the sting like some other, thinner, gloves have. Punching the ball is still possible with the fingersave *but* I rarely punch the ball.

The only thing I dislike is how they have the fingersave build into the thumb. It presses in on the top and side of the nail bed and is uncomfortable. I haven't found a way to push it down 1/2 inch and certainly can't change the angle. The left glove fits like, well, a glove and I barely notice the same thing but still notice it. Instead of a hard edge they might need to change the layout of the fingersave.

Normally I wear an Adidas or Reusch and this may be pushing Reusch out and into my new favorite. If I can figure a way out to warm up and melt the thumb fingersave to put a little curve into it, this would be the perfect glove.

I do not wash my gloves so haven't had any issues with the dye. I will gently wipe down the latex and the back of the glove unless the glove gets muddy. There are some renewal products that bring the tackiness back to the latex but I have not tried them with this glove.
text_fidelity_b: Renegade GK Fury Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 6-11, 7 Styles, Level 4) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 4+3MM Giga Grip | High Performance Pro-Level Goalkeeper Glove | Based in The USA

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker I'm a Fitbit lover. I track everything with it; steps, heart rate, activity, sleep, food, BMI, body fat. All these metrics warm my geeky little heart and help me achieve my health goals. I own a Flex, an Alta HR, and the Aria 2 scale and have adored all of them. Because I love them so much, I gave my husband a Charge 3 for his birthday. I'm sorry to say, this Fitbit product is a total dud. The tracker will not sync with Fitbit's app. It worked for about 1 month then just stopped syncing with the app. We've tried every flavor of delete-reinstall-reset possible, all to no avail. There are hundreds, maybe thousands, of people who have this same issue, who have reported it to Fitbit, and the response is unfortunately not in keeping with the company's usual excellent customer service. All they will offer people is another Charge 3. You can't even swap the tracker for a less expense, older model that works with their app. Without the app, without the ability to track and review a history, the Charge 3 is little better than the freebie plastic pedometers your employer's health insurance plan hands out at their annual Open Enrollment fair. What's more than a little irksome is that Fitbit seems unwilling to admit there's a major software problem here. Seems obvious when one reads the Help forums. Why not 'fess up and tell us an estimate of when we can expect a software update? I don't get it. People will likely be patient and wait for the update if they know one is in the works. What is to be gained by pretending nothing is wrong? A lot of very unhappy customers, that's what.

Long story short: Don't buy this tracker. Get a different one. Maybe even one not made by Fitbit (sorry, Fitbit!)
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker

text_fidelity_a:
Senyoo IP68 Waterproof Portable Camping Lamp and Rechargeable Emergency Light This was somebody's good idea, and I like it. We all have too many little handy gadgets that make our lives easier while also proliferating USB cables like rabbits and, in aggregate, taking up a lot of space.

The idea of making a lantern that also is a power bank for charging or running USB-compatible devices is GREAT. Why would you take both a lantern and a separate power bank along with you if you don't have to? If everyone on your trip has one of these as a personal light for hiking trails, there will be a lot of juice among you!

This lantern on the power-saving (dimmer) white light setting is gracious plenty light to read by, at least for me, and the bright light is quite good for seeing in the dark while on a trail. You can carry it as a light stick or stand it up on its charging end; the two USB ports, one standard, one mini, are tucked inside a screw-on cap that keeps it all waterproof until you take the cap off. On the on/off end (the green button as shown), there is a convenient wire hanging loop plus a lanyard (I received two) for looping it onto a belt, tactical bag, or tent loop. The red strobing lights serve as emergency lights. One of them flashes in a particular fast/slow sequence that reminds me of Morse code, so I wonder if it's not flashing a specific SOS-type signal. (Senyoo, can you clarify?)

The only thing I wish this had that it doesn't is a way to stow its USB charging cable. Throw in an alarm clock—or an ear-splitting alarm for the night joggers among us in case we are attacked—and this would truly be the Swiss army knife of lanterns. But it's already pretty great as it is. I was given this product in exchange for my unbiased review.
text_fidelity_b: Senyoo IP68 Waterproof Portable Camping Lamp and Rechargeable Emergency Light

text_fidelity_a:
SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag Waterproof Accessory for Paddle Boarding If the devil is in the details this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag is made with a range of details that make it an outstanding, well thought out bag, and should be perfect for our Kayaking and SUPing trips. We haven’t been out on the water yet this year, but cannot wait to get back out and without doubt, this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag will be going along for the ride! When I had the chance to grab this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag I decided to so we had a nice bag to carry those things we might need on the water and have a place to keep our phone, wallets, and keys safe. I am so glad I did - and my wife is thrilled. This bag was designed by someone who has time on the water and it shows.

The materials are top notch and the construction equally great. You can tell by looking at the bag the materials are good. But get your hands on it and you feel it. The thickness, the strength, the stitching - it all comes together and promises longevity. We always pay attention to zippers and in this case, not only is the handle-zipper strong and secure, but it settles in perfectly so as to keep water out. There are the details here - straps on the back top at each side so you can grab and hold on as you “try” to open and close the zipper. It literally warns you it is a hard pull and it is! That simply means water is going to be working hard to get in there. And the straps do help pull it across - though you’re still going to be grabbing the bag at some point to help. It is that tight! No problem if it means protecting your gear. They even included zipper lube so you can keep those zippers in top condition - something to keep in mind when you’re on fresh or salt water! Really impressive they thought of these things!

The strap for carrying it is also well done, with good materials, good stitching, and a comfortable padding on the shoulder. The straps for attaching to the SUP or Kayak are strong and well secured - they should last a good long time. Additionally, the rope on the top front allows you to secure things like towels, tighten it down, and keep them secure. An included wet bag for your phone gives added protection for that special need-to-have equipment.

Overall, this is a great, well designed bag that I think anyone who spends time on the water will appreciate. Well thought out, well constructed, and well executed, you are going to find any number of reasons to have it with - on the SUP or kayak, at the pool, beach, or wherever you spend time. We have not tested the waterproof aspect - again, haven’t been to the water yet, but while we appreciate the promise, we always still try to keep things dry. We would likely use other smaller dry bags inside - just to be safe - but appreciate the effort here. In the end, we are thrilled to have this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag.
text_fidelity_b: SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag Waterproof Accessory for Paddle Boarding

I still use my combination cable lock to lock my trunk pack and wheel. I put this U-lock around the bike rack and bike frame and use it to lock my helmet, too. This U-lock will not fit around my Electra Townie frame plus through the wheel, but that is probably just because of the Townie design, not a drawback to this lock.

This lock weighs about 5 pounds, so carrying it is a bit of a pain. I don't trust a mounting bracket for something this heavy. I put the U part of the lock inside the rack trunk and bungee the heavy bottom part either to the rack behind the seat, where it fits perfectly right behind the seat (perpendicular to the length of the rack). I use two of those bungee cords with the balls on the ends, instead of the hooks, because it seems safer in case they bust loose. I can also put the heavy part under the elastic bands on the top of my one-pocket trunk rack if I'm in a hurry, and it holds it securely, but then it wants to crush my little lunch (which is pretty small, since now I need to lose 5 pounds ;)

REDESS 11 Pack Exercise Resistance Bands with Handles Exercise Stretch Fitness Home Set Include 5 Stackable Exercise Bands with Carry Bag, Handles, Legs Ankle Straps & Door Anchor FINAL UPDATE - I ordered a Fitfort set, which has the same function as this package but doesn't seem destined to fail. I donated this set to Salvation Army the day Fitfort arrived. End of story.

UPDATE - After 4 months, the nylon bands on one handle failed. I'm improvising with rope earlier, the attachment to one band had to be fixed, and the black band has now torn. Was this worth four months' gym membership?

After one use, I find this adequate. I find good all-around routines, inlcuding one for straps, on darebee.

This kit provides a lot more resistance than the latex straps I'd been using. And the concept of being able to adjust your resistance by combining the five bands is good in principle. It's clear this will work better if you have good technique—slow, smooth movements, not jerky Yanks. But the small problems add up:

The concept is cool, but not unique. Post-COVID, there are a lot of these packs available, many for $10-15 less. Consider them!

Many reviews cite the handles as a weak point, and it's clear they will fail in time. They lasted fine through the first workout. (See below.)

These bands give different levels of resistance, but I'm not sure how much. There are 2 contradictory weight schemes in the Amazon posting (diff weights, diff color). Hint: blue is stronger than green. Also, I have no confidence that the numerical values are right. Is black really 40/50 pounds? Either I'm really strong...

Reviewers also reported snapped bands, and maybe it might be good to warm them up with a stretch before your workout. I believe the black and blue will snap if I stretch from from the floor to overhead, no I will have to kneel for military presses. And move smoothly thru your exercises, don't jerk or yank. It's better form, and will avoid snapping.

The Velcro ankle straps? Ha! Loop them through and they are secure!

UPDATE after 3 months: this set works, but it's not durable. One of the handles will tear, and then I'll have to re-sew it. The black band came loose from one of its hooks, and I re-fit it. The convenient carrying sack is fraying, like the ankle bands. This has been a lifeline during the lockdown that made my gym unsafe, but this is not a long-term fitness tool. It just won't last.

(CAUTION - the high rating for this set is because the reviews are mixed with what must be a very good beanie. Users of this set average 1-2 stars.)
text_fidelity_b: REDESS 11 Pack Exercise Resistance Bands with Handles Exercise Stretch Fitness Home Set Include 5 Stackable Exercise Bands with Carry Bag, Handles, Legs Ankle Straps & Door Anchor

MinnKota Riptide 55 ST Bowmount Trolling Motor with i-Pilot and No Foot Pedal (55lbs Thrust, 54" Shaft) I bought one of these for my 18' Carolina Skiff. I also bought the quick release mount. I bought the quick release mount so I could remove the trolling motor when travelling long distances with the boat. I fish from MD to the Gulf and bouncing down the road wouldn't be be good for it. First impression is that I'm going to like it a lot. I've been in the water twice using the trolling motor, both times in salt water, which is where I spend most of my fishing time. Installation was easy and deploying and retracting the ST55 is also easy. The iPilot anchor function worked well in 1.5 mph currents and 12 knot winds. I'll try it in the 8kt currents in the OBX in August. I like the iPilot control unit and no foot pedal because I'm not restricted to a certain place in the boat. I maxed it out and was surprised at how strong the motor was. I used the motor for about 2 hours and battery drain was about 1.4 volts from 14.2 to 12.8. Totally acceptable, especially for the size boat and winds. The instructions call for a 60 amp inline circuit breaker, however, I'm using a 40 amp and it was fine on full power. I've given it a 4 star rating right now and will return to add more to this review once I've used the programming features of the iPilot.

Update 24 Feb 15: I have nothing but praise for Min-Kota and the RipTide ST55. I've put about 70 hours on this motor and spent many hours in the anchor mode against 2-3 knot tides. I didn't use my boat anchor once during the summer and fall months because the RipTide's anchor function is spot on. I mainly fish in saltwater and I've used it from Florida, to North Carolina, to Maryland and its performance is outstanding. The only down side is it doesn't have automatic deploy and retrieve. I know Min-Kota is working on one. I love the iPilot! I can use it from anywhere on the boat and only have to remember when facing backwards, left is right and right is left. Duh. Most definitely 5 STARS
text_fidelity_b: MinnKota Riptide 55 ST Bowmount Trolling Motor with i-Pilot and No Foot Pedal (55lbs Thrust, 54" Shaft)

text_fidelity_a:
Lanzom® Outdoor Camouflage Bucket Hats Mesh Sun Hat Boonie Fishing Hats The orange hat I ordered was SO UGLY that I actually had to order a different color (the navy) for myself at full price so I could write a fair review. I was fortunate to be able to purchase the orange one at a discount and I was hoping to receive the bright, punchy tangerine color shown in the example image. Instead I received a burnt orange hat with a bright orange mesh band and all of it is HIDEOUS. I was so upset that I had "wasted" my discount! Luckily my 9 year old is willing to wear the hat which is good because I can't return it. I can promise you this orange hat will never be stolen. EVER.

The pictures I included were taken in natural daylight and they don't accurately capture just how ugly and mis-matched the orange hat is. The body of the hat is a burnt blood orange color. It is remarkably ugly, even for University of Texas fans. The mesh band is safety orange - very similar to the neon orange color deer hunters sometimes wear. In person, the colors clash so badly that it really is only appropriate for a 9 year old boy to wear because it is assumed he doesn't know any better. And even then it is only suitable to wear fishing. Alone, so no one sees the hat. On a windy lake where you have the best chance of losing it.

The Navy hat is a million times better. It, too, does not match its example image but in a good way. The hat is a deep, dark midnight navy shade with a dark navy band that matches the hat body. It looks very nice. If I could do it over again I would select the black or navy for myself. Anything but this orange hat!

The hat itself is very comfortable and lightweight. I love the feel of it, how breathable it is and that the strap is very loose and lightweight. (I can't stand the feeling of things around my chin and neck or the sensation that cords are choking me.) This hat is pleasantly comfortable, bounces back from being crushed (or thrown across the room and trampled underfoot until the navy hat arrived because it was so danged ugly) and it seems like it will shed water well if splashed.

I was fortunate to be able to purchase this hat at a discount, I just picked the wrong color. I liked the hat well enough to buy it at full price in another color that I am actually willing to wear. I REALLY wished I had bought any color but the orange! I hope that by sharing my experience and photos that you are able to make the best buying decision! (Hint: ORANGE is the wrong answer!)
text_fidelity_b: Lanzom® Outdoor Camouflage Bucket Hats Mesh Sun Hat Boonie Fishing Hats

text_fidelity_a:
Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle I've had this bike a few months now. It is quiet (but not silent, there is a noise from the drive belt) but it is very smooth and responsive.

Assembly was straight-forward, but unless you want to find all the tools you need to assemble it yourself, I would recommend getting the tool package available on their website. The torque wrench was our deciding factor in just buying their kit. Keiser offers a discount on the tool package if you purchase it with the bike directly on their website.

Things to know: the app is TERRIBLE. Other reviewers have already listed all the bugs in depth, but the app is unreliable for recording workouts and is not user-friendly. The bike also will not work directly with other apps (like Peloton). For that you need the converter, which costs another $200 on top of this bike, unless you buy the bike directly from their website. Then it is only $50. Considering they were discounting it 75% with purchase of the bike, I consider $200 a rip-off for what your bike should have done in the first place (work with other apps). I wrote customer service about the bugs. They agreed there was a problem and the developer would be notified. I was told I would be updated when it was fixed. I never was. The problem in the app still persists as of my writing this review.

Customer service: I wrote customer service via email. As far as timeliness, they wrote back quickly. However, if I ever had more than one question in my message, one, and only one, of my questions would be answered. I had to write back multiple times for my additional questions to be answered, so one simple email took several days to be fully addressed. As stated above, some of the issues never were.

I will update the review if any issues with the bike itself come up. I love the bike, how smooth it runs, and the huge range of resistances available. It seems well-designed and like it will hold up. However, there are some big annoyances that will cost you extra $$$ to overcome.
text_fidelity_b: Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle

text_fidelity_a:
ALGOMA 2781SPC Quick Dry Hammock, 13-Feet, Earth Tones We were so looking forward to receiving this hammock - but when it arrived, our hopes and dreams were dashed to the ground like refuse thrown into a gutter! The hammock took longer than expected to arrive - but not to worry-- we patiently checked Amazon tracking on a daily basis to see when the refreshment of lying on a soft, sturdy hammock whilst sipping a cocktail - would arrive at our door. After waiting on the edge of our plastic lawn chairs for two weeks, the big day finally arrived! The hammock was delivered by our friendly Amazon courier and shouts of joy could be heart resounding through the halls of our home! Two of our sons ceremoniously carried the long hammock box into the house like a wealthy Roman patron being carried through the streets on a litter. The box was opened and said hammock was unrolled like a precious scroll. Visions of hours spent snoozing under a canopy of trees danced in the heads of family members as they clamored to put this 'Object of 'Liesure and Rest' onto the stand that had carried our old, canvas, LL BEAN hammock. After 14 years of service, that good sanctuary had finally rotted away. (Actually, I wasn't home for this part, but I'm sure this is how it went.)

Our faithful and strong sons set the hammock up beneath towering Tulip Populars, wafting in the refreshing breeze and waited for me to come home hoping to unveil a pleasant surprise for the beloved mother. I arrived home, hot, sweaty and tired from a long day of horseback riding with my faithful steed. A persistent headache was pounding in my brain from hours of tracking desperados through the forests. (Ok, I was actually trying to catch up to my friends who had galloped away rather prematurely.) Anyway, as I slogged through the house, wilted and exhausted, my god-like son winked at me whilst ushering me through the back door to the paradise that awaited in the back yard.

THERE IT WAS! THE HAMMOCK for which I had been longing! I sat down on the side and stretched my battered frame onto the hammock like Cleopatra reclining under a gold-embroidered canopy dressed as Aphrodite, (but wearing riding boots and half-chaps).....only to discover that the hammock of my dreams was an imposter!!!! THIS WAS NO SOFT BED OF ROSES TO LIE ON! NO! IT FELT LIKE BAD CARPET ON THE WALLS OF A CHEAP MOTEL! I stifled my revulsion and tried to get comfortable but it was no use. The fabric wasn't fabric at all - it felt like plastic water bottles woven into a nightmarish tapestry by well-intentioned environmentalists! I leapt from this bed of vipers disgusted and disappointed. My family pleaded with me to give it another chance, saying "It's not so bad, we like it!" "Philistines!!!!" I retorted! " THIS. WILL. NOT. DO!" whilst gnashing my teeth to the best of my ability. To which they shrugged and got the box out of the trash so we could return it.

Postscript - If you want a comfy hammock made out of sunbrella fabric, you have to spend about $250 these days. I found one on Wayfair and now we are anxiously awaiting that one to be delivered. Cheers! :)
text_fidelity_b: ALGOMA 2781SPC Quick Dry Hammock, 13-Feet, Earth Tones

Other coolers collapse more when put into storage. This one is not designed to be collapsed, although it can be smooshed into a smaller shape when not in use. Good coolers can last many years, so you might want to invest in a high-quality one.

Fitinfuser Fruit Flavor Infuser Water Bottles with Insulating Sleeve and Mixing Spring Ball I received this as a free review sample. I am going to address the reason I subtracted a star up front: the vessel is made from two pieces that are plastic 'welded' together. For normal use in controlled environments this is not an issue. However, I've owned bottles made from the same material and construction that literally split apart when dropped on concrete.

The main reason why I still rated this so highly is while I own water bottles with this capacity this is the first infuser that is a full 32 ounces (that I know about.) Since my favorite way of hydrating is with infused apples, stick cinnamon and a touch of honey, this is perfect for me. I especially like the large infusing basket.

While the product description claims you can use it with hot or old beverages take my word for it that although it will hold hot liquid, you do not want to use it for that. The main reason is it's difficult to handle. On the other hand, it can be run through a dishwasher (although you need to put the cap in the top tray.)

Accessing the drinking spout requires that you release the stainless U-shaped bail, which locks the cap closed and helps to prevent leaks. Plus, this is totally leak-proof. I tried in vain to make it leak when I was testing it out and it is a tight seal.

The side grips - one made from what looks like silicone and the opposite textured into the vessel - make handling this large bottle easy. Had another silicone piece been used in lieu of the textured pattern you probably could use this with hot liquids in a safe manner. This fit the console cup holders in my 2014 Mitsubishi Outlander, but is too tall to fit into the driver and passenger door cup holders (it's about 9.5 inches tall with the cap on.)

Bottom line: if you work in a controlled environment (carpeted floors, etc.) and love to hydrate with infused drinks this is ideal. I would not recommend it for outdoors and harsh environments unless you are extra careful.
text_fidelity_b: Fitinfuser Fruit Flavor Infuser Water Bottles with Insulating Sleeve and Mixing Spring Ball

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Apex XT Bike Hitch Rack I ordered the ‘Thule Apex XT Swing 4 Bike Hitch Rack’ for review. I liked that the design of the Thule Apex XT which allows you to swing the rack (while installed and loaded) out and away, so that you can open your back hatch while your bikes are installed on the rack. My other hitch style bike rack does not allow this, and I have to remove the bikes to access my back hatch. I have assembled, installed and used the Thule Apex XT bike rack for some time now and would like to share my thoughts.

I would firstly like to get out of the way some of the other complaints I have read about the assembly of this particular Thule bike rack. Basically it comes shipped in two main parts. The complaint is that the main bolt that connects these two parts was too tight and many people ended up breaking something and complained that the two parts and bolt did not assemble correctly. I would like to say that for me, (after reading the issues people were having) I was a bit concerned. BUT, I really had no issue at all. Yes it was a bit difficult to install the said bolt, but that is absolutely to be expected with the way the two pieces connect. Basically all I did was to line up the parts the best I could, stick the bolt in the top hole and slightly jiggle the rack assembly while putting downward pressure on the bolt until it fell into place. Yes it was a snug fit, but really there was no issue. After these two parts are assembled, there will be no need to take them apart again.

With that out of the way, I would like to say that I have never owned a Thule product but have always wanted to because of the brand reputation. So far in my opinion, this really is a quality product, however I do feel that it’s a bit overpriced compared to other brands out there that are also well built and of good quality and design. The features that this rack offers however, such as the “swing out” design, built in bike lock cable and easy hitch mount with lock included, makes this particular model very appealing and a feature packed value. I guess what I am trying to say is that there is absolute value to the Thule Apex XT bike rack if you could find it on sale.

Build quality in my opinion is great but I do notice that there is a lot of plastic and my concern would be, how well will it hold up over time? Fortunately the plastic parts used are not part of the main construction, rather more for cosmetics and if they do crack or break, it shouldn’t affect the functionality of the bike rack itself.

Others have mentioned, and I have noticed it myself that there is a bit of rattle in the unit but because of the way it’s designed, that is inevitable. It’s not going to fall apart or off your hitch for that matter as long as you have assembled it correctly of course but the rattle is noticeable.

Now for the ONLY real issue I have is that my daughters (oddly shaped) 26” frame does not fit on this rack unfortunately. I know that there is an adapter that is available from Thule, but I honestly don’t think that it would work with the way her frame is designed. All of our other bikes work great and securely with this rack, but if I am to take her bike, I will have to use my other rack.

Overall, I think this is a well made quality “hitch mount” bike rack with great features but beware that some bikes won’t fit, and you may be better off with another model that supports the bikes from the tires which will allow more compatibility.

text_fidelity_a:
Flasite Hoola-Hoop-Weighted-for-Adults-and-Kids - Weight Loss Pilates Trainer Circle 27 Sections Detachable Knots Fitness& Massage Abdomen Exercise Hoops I've been using this for about two weeks now. It does what I bought it to do and I have a lot of fun using it, but there are certain flaws that lead me to say it's overpriced.

First the good: it's easy to put together and works as advertised. It took me a few tries to find the right fit (a little tighter than I first thought) and several practice attempts before I could get the weight spinning long enough for a good workout (but I was never that great at regular hula hoops as a kid). Playing with the length of the cord also resulted in a much better workout, and the catch is very strong; it holds whatever length I set no matter how hard or long I use it.

Snapping the links into position was moderately challenging, but my grip strength is relatively poor so no surprise there. Opening and closing the hoop for actual use is easy, and that's what's important. There's a novelty factor to this, of course, but I do find it fun to use, which motivates me to use it regularly.

Now the not so good: a few of the pieces arrived broken. Although I don't need those links now, it's disappointing that I won't have them in the future if need be.

A bigger issue is that this thing is loud -- not "wake the neighbors" loud but loud enough to disturb others in the house. I wasn't expecting it to be utterly silent, but neither was I expecting this rattling. This limits my use of it somewhat.

I got this as a cardio option other than walking or biking. I have posterior tibial tendonitis -- a fancy way of saying tendonitis of the ankle/foot; walking or running for long distances can irritate it, and biking isn't always an option for me. The weighted hula hoop is a very good alternative to these activities because I can get a good cardio workout without aggravating my PTT. Admittedly, I can't go as long with this as I can walking or biking, but I can make it a lot more intense. Besides, this is still kind of new to me, and I'm confident that I can build my stamina over time. Judging from the feel of the materials, though, I'm not sure how durable this device will be.

Prices here vary all the time, of course. I got this for about $35 altogether. Given the breakage, I'd say that was slightly overpriced; I certainly wouldn't advise anyone to pay more than that for this. It's a nice tool for your home gym, but I'd wait to buy it on sale or at least until February when most of us have left our new year's resolutions in the dust.
text_fidelity_b: Flasite Hoola-Hoop-Weighted-for-Adults-and-Kids - Weight Loss Pilates Trainer Circle 27 Sections Detachable Knots Fitness& Massage Abdomen Exercise Hoops

The insulation is nothing short of magical - water with a few cubes stays as cold as the Grinch's cold, cold heart. I haven't tried the heat-retention capability, but I don't doubt that it would keep hot beverages suitably warm, if not downright hellish.

The Flip Cap lid on the version I bought is allegedly for hot beverages, but it works very well with cold water for me. The straw lid never seemed appealing to me - who wants to make that oh-so-subtle end of beverage sucking sound just when their boss asks them for a thought or two in a staff meeting? The Sport Cap is fairly intimidating - it looks like I'd need to take a certification class before understanding it. And the wide mouth flat cap apparently has to be completely removed for drinking.

The color I chose is called Plum, but it's pretty much a run-of-the-mill purple - I had been hoping for a whiff of periwinkle, but am happy enough with the plummy goodness I have.

I did buy an add-on non-Hydro Flask strap to make carrying easier - I'm aiming for all-hands-free all-the-time in my accessories by the end of 2018.

text_fidelity_a:
Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire I purchased Campy Shamal 2-way rims a couple years back. I then purchased everything needed to mount and maintain tubeless tires including Fusion 3s. I ride a '12 Specialized S-Works Roubaix and mostly do fast training rides about 3 to 4 days a week with longer rides beyond 60 miles fairly regularly. I weigh out at roughly 185 pounds.

Tubeless and ceramic bearings are somewhat in the same category these days in terms of bikers wondering if this equipment truly makes a difference. Well, I've ridden ceramic bearings in my crank and in my wheels...and YES...it makes a difference...now...I've ridden on tubeless for two riding seasons...and YES...they make a difference. Tubeless is the future...as it is in nearly every vehicle that has wheels from a riding mower to a motorcycle to a car...and mountain bikes. Why it has taken so long with road biking is understandable...change is hard...and manufacturers will go where the money is.

First, let me make this clear...putting the Fusion 3 tires on was a chore...and I mean...a CHORE. It will test your patience. Do NOT succumb to using levers as it will ruin the bead. Google tubeless tire installation for help but even then it will baffle you as to how you're going to get that tire over the rim...but...you will...and the benefits will be worth it.

Second, it takes a few rides to get the tires truly seated. Use an air compressed pump if you've got it...but...I had a "Joe Blow" floor pump that worked fine. I didn't install the sealant until after the second short ride and pump up. You will most likely lose quite a bit of air at first but as the tire seals over time...the air pressure stabilized. I do pump up my tires before every ride but it isn't out of the norm of my former clincher tires.

Third, I've ridden my fusion 3s at 90psi on the front tire and 100psi on the back. The ride is fast & super smooth. A lot of riders think super high psi is better but that is, (arguably for some), not true because at a high psi your tire is actually bumping up and down off the road which drains energy transfer over time. The benefit of running tubeless at lower psi is that the tire remains in more constant contact with the road which...over time...equals better energy transfer...and hence...speed, comfort, and endurance. Also, there is some evidence that without a tube you eliminate friction...I'm honestly not sure about that claim...even so, I can say from experience that I'm not going back to tubed tires...tubeless tires run as advertised.

Fourth, durability...I run typical roads here in Maryland over countless miles...up and down hills...less maintained side roads...and these Fusion 3s can go yet another season. The wear is normal with no unusual issues. I've NOT had one flat tire. I've NOT added more sealant since the first install...which I should've done...but...it hasn't made a difference.

Fifth, the only reservation I have is getting a flat tire but I guess it's a good thing that I'm not as use to dealing with flats like I had for my tubed tires. I have to say it has been a pleasure to not have had one flat for two seasons.

I'd like to try the ATOM version of this tire...and I think I'll get it just for comparison purposes. Not looking forward to the install and my expectation is that they will not fit my riding style, endurance expectations, and my higher weight...even so, I'm a believer in trying anything once...so...we'll see.

All in all...educate yourself but don't be afraid to go tubeless. It is change that we all seem to avoid but I'll never go back now that I've tried it out...and as the biking money goes...tubeless quality and selection will as well. ENJOY!
text_fidelity_b: Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire

text_fidelity_a: East West U.S.A D3031 31" Sports Duffle Gym Travel Gear Bag My first impression... it is much lower quality than I was expecting. I paid much much less than that so I'm not too disappointed. If I was to fill the bag full with moderate weight items I don't think the bag would hold up long.  It has a lot of space, I'd estimate it could over the SHORT-term maybe handle up to 50 pounds. With a bag this size you could easily reach that weight.  On the other hand, this bag will work awesome for lightweight bulky objects, I could see myself throwing a rolled yoga mat, a couple towels, change of clothes, pair of shoes, and a bunch of other stuff in it and still have some room.  I'd be hesitant to use this as luggage although maybe it would work for just for car trips.  I think it will work great for storing bulky comforters or blankets for the summer.  Most of the 31 inch length is the main compartment and the zippered opening opens big and wide.  The end compartments each take up only a few inches of the full length. Again I was very impressed with the large size. It appears much larger in person than the picture. If it's stuffed full the proportions will probably be similar to what's pictured.

I didn't even want to try another one, but to get my partner to agree to go camping I had to supply an air mattress so I went with the one with the highest rating within my budget and waited to be disappointed. Imagine my surprise. You can charge the pump from your vehicle (no batteries! which was great because they didn't even cross my mind) or from a regular outlet. The pump is noisy but not unusually so, and the mattress inflated pretty darn quick. It was ample for 2 large people and 2 small dogs. Best of all, incredibly, it didn't deflate overnight! I did "top it off" a bit for the 3rd night but over-all it was full and comfy, survived excited dogs and 40 degree weather, the pump has a reverse so you can deflate it really fast, and somehow, someway, it actually all fit back easily into the box it came in so we can keep it safe for next time. It wasn't even overpoweringly stinky like plastic usually is (we still aired it out of course, how stinky is too stinky being quite subjective but neither of us was bothered).  If someone asked me to recommend an air mattress, I would gleefully direct them to this one.

text_fidelity_a: BBAhandware 27.7x18.2x16 in Folding Table Portable Large Camping Table Ultra Light Folding Beach Table Camping with Carrying Bag,Withstands Weights of Up to 55lbs (Silver) I'm not a serious prepper or anything, but I did live 5 days last February without power during the blizzard in Texas.  I have spent the subsequent months getting ready for another time like that again.  The video I watched was a cool way to heat an area in your house when the power is off.  I already had the rectangular paving stones/bricks to place on this table as well as the little alcohol burners.  The idea is to place the cement stones/bricks (the flat ones, not the large ones with holes in them) around the alcohol burner.  The alcohol burner transfers heat to the bricks which in turn release the stored heat over a longer time in the area where they are set up.  Obviously this can't be set up on the floor, so a table that can handle the stored heat is what I needed.  I set the cement blocks up on this metal camping table, put the alcohol burner in the middle and let it "work."  This camping table is the perfect size for my emergency room warming set up with the bricks an burner.  I know it will work fine for a table to use my propane cookstove on as well, but for the moment it is in an emergency box in my house along with the cement bricks and the alcohol burner (and a bottle of rubbing alcohol).  I'm very happy with how this table worked out for my purposes.
text_fidelity_b: BBAhandware 27.7x18.2x16 in Folding Table Portable Large Camping Table Ultra Light Folding Beach Table Camping with Carrying Bag,Withstands Weights of Up to 55lbs (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Breakfast and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply Everyday Meals 4 Gallon Pail & Butter Powder 2 lbs 4 oz No. 10 Can I'm buying calories. I am buying calories to tuck away for use after all other calories have been consumed. I have this and know it is available. I dont need to worry about it. It is there as part of my "calorie savings account". Not worried about taste, not worried about anything other than calories- preferably a variety of flavors with a good ratio of macros (fat, protein, carbohydrates). Emergency food is what it is, and what it will be. With increasing prices, todays caloric purchase is a savings over tomorrows.

So no, I haven't tried it. I HAVE used other Augason Farms products for daily life use and have been pleased. I regularly buy Augason Farms (best price point, best sales). I have tried those items only because the sale price was better than buying non emergency packed food items. I use a lot of tomato powder, dehydrated vegetables, protein crumbles, etc.. and once in awhile a sale will work in my favor. That is when I will buy 2 of something. One for now, one for way later. Rinse and repeat.

Certain food items have at least 25 year shelf life, some items are 10 years. No matter, I will eat it all 30 years down the line if need be. Foods dont just go "bad". The date is not a safety issue. It is a quality issue. So maybe the smell, taste, texture, or vitamin content alters a little over time, but it is still edible. Calories are still there.

If you want to be sure of a tasty meal that is within the best by date range, then simple stack your pantry with foods that you know and love. Rotate. Have a "working pantry" that you grab from on a daily basis, then have a "storage pantry" that works as your own in home "store". It also serves as your emergency preps. When you need to pull from your storage pantry, be sure to replace. Keep adding to it, one or two cans at a time. one or two bags of something at a time. Emergency food does not need to be emergency packaged food (prices are higher for the packaging, uniformity, processing etc). If "emergency" packaged food is outside your budget, then dont bother. If it is something you are keen on, then look for sales regularly (maybe daily) and buy when the good price strikes. Of course, you can look into creating your own long term storage meals too (mylar, oxy absorbers, pails, etc).

Just.. have something. Dont be someone who has bare shelves and scoffs at preparedness because emergency meals taste bad. Nah, buy what is good to you, buy what is affordable to you, buy basic stuff or buy fancy emergency stuff. But have stuff. Prices aren't coming down, prices will continue to go up, food will be harder to come by. So at the very least consider it an investment. And if there is a true need for it in terms of *vaguely gestures around* all else that is going on (weather events, political events, ww3, etc) then you wont be scrambling, begging off neighbors, stealing, etc.

So current $60 for nearly 20,000 calories of a variety of food? Not too shabby in light of everything. (same $60 can buy a lot more calories, but be sure to store well for max "freshness").
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Breakfast and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply Everyday Meals 4 Gallon Pail & Butter Powder 2 lbs 4 oz No. 10 Can

Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow Good anti stress eye pillow. What I like about the Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy pillow
1) I like the fragrance of the lavender and chamomile pillow.
2) The fragrance is not overwhelming it is subtle.
3) It is not overstuffed so it drapes nicely over your eye and sinus area when you are lying flat.
4) The silk has a cooling effect
5) I have chronic sinusitis and this pillow feels like it helps to relieve some of that tight pressure pain. It also seems to calm the area around my eyes.
I have used several different sinus pillow type remedies over the years for that "ahhh relief!" moment when you can feel the swelling and ache diminishing.Not many were very effective but this one and the Lavender eye pillow by AyaZen are both effective. However, I would choose the one from AyaZen over this one because:
1) It can be heated and froze as long as you put it in a plastic sealed bag so it doesn't absorb freezer odor.
2) It has more filling and a more balanced filling making it a little weightier than the Earth Therapeutics eye pillow
3) The velvet like cover of the AyaZen is soft and luxurious yet it also has a griping effect so it doesn't readily slip off your face.
4) It has a stronger lavender scent that is soothing but not overwhelming.
5) For me, this pillow relieves the pain and pressure associated with my sinusitis better.

As a comparison, they are both good eye pillows but AyaZen wins for me.

The reason Earth Therapeutics is not a perfect five stars and doesn't win for me:
1) It doesn't have the balanced filling the AyaZen does
2) The silk used to encase the Earth Therapeutics pillow slips very easily unless you are lying down flat.If your head happens to turn a little while sleeping at an angle or with your head raised at any height, it slips off. Even though you can conform it to your eyes and nose it won't stay because of the silkiness of the material and the almost whisper light weight of the pillow. If your head is raised at any angle or your head happens to fall sideways while napping, you must continually reposition the pillow.
3) you cannot heat it in the microwave or put it in the freezer. I know this pillow is suppose to be Therapeutic based solely on the oils it harbors and the silk that encases it but it just needs a little more to really reach that Therapeutic level.

I bought this based on it conforming to the face and being Therapeutic. However, I often sleep with my head raised up or in my recliner because of breathing issues due to my sinuses.The silk of this pillow would always cause it to slip down or sideways causing me to wake up and recenter it on my eyes. Overall, I would recommend this pillow for someone who doesn't have to sleep with the head or upper body raised at any height and doesn't have to turn their head much while napping. The silk does have a cooling effect and the lavender and chamomile does help to relieve some of the pressure and pain.

Joby Gorillatorch Blade Tactical Flashlight I was highly impressed with this flashlight. It is a nice, clean design, and the adjustable tripod allows you to put the light right where you need it, especially in tight places such as in the interior of a computer. The rear switch is perfect for carrying the light in your fist and working with your thumb. A real plus: it has flat sides so when you put it down it does not roll away!

The light itself is very bright (I almost want to advise "Do not look into light with remaining eyeball"), especially on the highest setting. You can adjust the aperture for a wide or a narrow beam. We have inadequate lighting in our back yard, which extends back at least 15 yards (probably more), and using this flashlight in almost total darkness I could see the details of the trees and back fence while walking our dog.

USB charging is very convenient, since it is now such a universal technology. When plugged in to charge, the unit glows blue until done, so it's very easy to know when its finished. This is an excellent piece of equipment for use in an emergency kit or just for plain everyday use.

Downsides: the rear cover over the charging port and the switch seem flimsy, and there's no way to change out the battery that I can find (nor is it mentioned in the manual). However, I would still highly recommend this product.
text_fidelity_b: Joby Gorillatorch Blade Tactical Flashlight

BE REALLY CAREFUL WHEN FILLING. This valve adapter has no step down feature for tank pressure. IF YOU HOOK IT UP TO YOUR PCP GUN, AND CRANK THE SCUBA TANK VALVE FULL OPEN, YOU WILL BLOW THE SEALS OUT ON YOUR GUN. ALL IT TAKES IS TO BARELY, AND CAUTIOUSLY OPEN THE TANK VALVE.

Do I recommend it? Absolutely. Just use caution when filling your rifle or pistol, unless you LOVE replacing seals. I found a used, and recently VIP-ed Aluminum 80 (3300 PSI) for $99 at my local dive shop. That’s a lot better than the $400 and $500 tanks and valves sold by air gun outlets.

text_fidelity_a:
90 Degree By Reflex High Waist Fleece Lined Leggings with Side Pocket - Yoga Pants First of all, i bought this pants not entirely for yoga and thus i picked the one with pockets. I needed a pair of leggings with fleece that i can walk my dog during winter (in California!!). Don't judge me...but i am terrified of the cold. I bought the pants in two sizes, two colors; all with pockets.

FIT:
"M" and "S" fits me perfectly because the material is super stretchy and extremely comfortable. I'm 5'6 and 133lbs. "M" has the length that would wrap around the heel nicely and it doesn't feel bulky. I ended up taking the "S" simply because it was in black and i didn't want to take the trouble of returning. But on the hindsight, i would have preferred the "M" so i can pull it over my heel and not worry about wearing out the material over time.

COMFORT:
The fleece is very smooth and comfy. Definitely not a thin legging that you can wear underneath a pair of skinny jeans (unfortunately!). The pockets do add on the extra thickness.

WARMTH:
In an evening of ~50F, wearing just the leggings, socks and a pair of running shoes still left my feet feeling cold (again, don't judge the Californians..it's just me!). I couldn't walk my dog comfortably unless i start jogging to build up the heat. When I swapped my running shoes with a pair of Uggs/boots that gave me more coverage, it helped a lot. I've seen reviews where people would wear it outdoor in the snow under some snow pants... i dont know if I can make the same comparison.

Overall, i just love how comfortable the pants are. Not super expensive but also not as cheap.
text_fidelity_b: 90 Degree By Reflex High Waist Fleece Lined Leggings with Side Pocket - Yoga Pants

text_fidelity_a:
Long Western to English Leather Girth Converters I have spent endless hours trying to figure out how to convert a western saddle and a hybrid Brisbane Aussie saddle that uses a traditional D ring for rigging. Trust me, there’s more products that convert an English to western rigging but I was determined to call Australia and known saddlery companies to see if any product exists. I hit pay dirt here at Amazon after seeing them advertised at Elite Saddleworks in AU. Seems they sell their converters here at Amazon and my search is over.

As far as the product goes, these converter straps are beautifully made with heavy quality leather and a nice solid buckling system. So simple to use. Quite frankly, I did not think I was going to be able to find a correct product to make the conversion but I am delighted that these are on the market for those riders who do not like the typical Western strapping system for cinching. I find using a traditional English/Australian girth with a buckling system to be much safer for the rider and the horse… And you do not have to dismount to make any adjustments if the saddle becomes loose or needs re-positioning due to the girth.

So let me save you hours of trouble if you’re the type that has the rings on your saddle for cinching and you want to go to a buckled girth. My other suggestion is I bought at Amazon the ovation neoprene girth with elastic bands on one side and they are amazing for the price as the quality is excellent and very very comfortable for the horse. The only issue you may have is the sizing as if you read through the descriptions, some folks seem to see the girth being true to size and others suggest buying slightly larger.Other wonderful Amazon reviewer’s wrote me and made suggestions as far as finding the correct size if you have the saddle billets to measure from or actually taking a string and measuring the horses girth area. I didn’t take a chance and I actually bought four different sizes to make sure I found the correct size and will return the wrong sized ones. Looks like it’s a bit of a science as far as finding the right size for your horse or pony but the girth got incredible reviews and the price is exceptional for the value and the quality of the item..
text_fidelity_b: Long Western to English Leather Girth Converters

First off, NONE of the seams are sealed. I set the tent up and crawled into it to check it out. Pin holes, pin holes, and MORE pin holes. If you purchase this tent, and take it out without doing anything to it, you WILL get wet if it rains!! For sure!!
So I sealed all the seams with a good seam sealer.
Next, is the body of the tent. Not so sure how waterproof it is, especially after seeing all of the pin holes in the seams. So, I sprayed it down very good with Scotchguard silicone spray.
Then two of the poles are damaged. One looks like a water pipe after freezing damage, and the other looks like it was stomped on a few times. So, this tells me right off, that the QC team could care less!
When I took the tent down, the small wire retainers that are in the ends of the poles to keep them from falling apart, pulled out of the top end of the middle pole section, and stayed lodged in the upper pole section. Not good.
The side pull out tabs have NO inner reinforcement. So if you pull on the sides too hard, you could easily rip a hole in the side of the tent at the attachment points. should have been a piece of material sewn inside for additional strength.
The stakes are the cheap and heavy steel stakes. The aluminum stakes would have been much better and lighter.
All in all, IF you want to spend the extra time to waterproof this tent, it would be a good tent to use as a backpacking tent. Stansport really needs to up their game when it comes to this tent. I would have spent the extra $5 or $10 for the items that I have mentioned, and this tent would be easily be a 4 or 5 star tent!
UPDATE: After seam sealing the inside and outside of the tent, this tent STILL leaks. The main points of leakage are at the 6 stake out points on the floor. The floor is made of tarp material, and seam sealer will not stay adhered to this material. I even cleaned the spots to seam seal very well with alcohol to remove any residual chemicals that might interfere with adhesion. I would NOT recommend this tent. The ONLY thing this tent is good for, is good weather camping or as a childs play tent in the yard. If you are looking for a backpacking tent, DO NOT PURCHASE THIS ONE!! YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED.

UPDATE: After seam sealing and waterproofing this tent I set it up in my yard and tested it during a rain storm. Nothing serious, just your average rain storm. This tent STILL leaked. It failed miserably! Since the return window has passed, I guess I will be sticking this in my "Yard Sale" pile or letting the kids use it as a play tent. DO NOT waste your money on this tent! Total garbage!
text_fidelity_b: Stansport Scout 2 Person Tent

text_fidelity_a:
NCAA Kentucky Wildcats Can Cooler, 16 I have this exact same cooler from another team, and got this one as a gift for my cousin, who is a huge fan. This cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it! (I ended up buying everyone their favorite team's cooler in this same brand, and they were a huge hit over the holidays!)

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. Just make sure you get the one like this one from "TLG8," to get the high quality one I just described. Thanks for reading my review. Hope it helped someone.
text_fidelity_b: NCAA Kentucky Wildcats Can Cooler, 16

High Sierra Karadon Frame Pack, Amethyst/BlackBerry/Orchid, 30L (S-M) As far as looks go, this backpack is really nice! If a backpack can be called "lovely", I'd have to say that about this one. It's well made and appears very sturdy. It looks to be a high quality backpack.

I think all body types will be different, but for me, this backpack is comfortable to wear. The shoulders and hips have extra padding, so it doesn't rub into those parts. There's plenty of adjustable straps to make it more likely to fit each person just the way they need it to. The padding on the hips and shoulders are also removable, so you can (hand)wash those parts most likely to get sweaty and stinky. I haven't washed these parts yet, but right now they are attached very well. You have to really pull it to get it off, but it's not so hard that you're going to pull a muscle.

There's a rain guard attached within one of the pockets, so you can easily keep the backpack and your belongings dry if it rains. (This is the bottom pocket and the zipper is on the underside of the backpack.) There's extra room in there if you wanted to store anything with the rain guard. The middle space within the backpack is accessed from both the top and the middle, and it is open the whole length of the backpack. It is very roomy, and can be expanded with the 4 adjustable straps on the sides. (2 on each side) There's also a pocket behind the main one. Though it's not as roomy as the middle space, it still gives you lots of extra space. There's a pocket(without zippers or extras) on each side also. Each side of the hip strap has a little zippered pocket and one without a zipper. There's also a zippered pocket on the top cover. There's lots of adjustable straps all around, and also a couple of hooks.

Overall, this is a super nice and comfortable backpack, and I think most ladies will be extremely pleased with it.

Old Timer Generational USA Series Traditional Fixed and Folding Knives with 1095 HC Stainless Steel Blades, Sawcut Bone Handles, and Made in USA for Hunting, Skinning, EDC, Field Dressing, and Outdoor I have not previously worked with Old Timer knives, though I have had my share of pocket knives that have served me well. So, this is my first experience with this brand and so far I am very pleased. This is a quality pocket knife, without a lot of frills and fancy features but very well made and attractive.

Most cheap pocket knives have a plastic handle, spring-assisted fly-out blade, and a locking mechanism. Beyond that the features become quite varied and bring different features to the table. That's all good, but anything beyond the basics - a blade in a case - adds weight and size. This knife is different. It keeps everything very simple - a single pull-out blade that locks. That's it.

The blade is solid and sharp right out of the package and is well suited for most tasks. There is no wobble in the blade and it remains stiff and tight, which is a good thing. The blade is free of pits and dings (at least initially) and is sharp enough to cut without pain (so be careful).

The handle is bone, not cheap plastic or resin. It has a nice, solid feel to it and it will last for decades with proper care. It also has eye appeal and is reminiscent of old-fashioned knives.

I am very pleased with this knife and will carry it instead of a larger cheap knife when I want a small, lightweight but well-made knife with me. I expect to get years of service from this knife.
text_fidelity_b: Old Timer Generational USA Series Traditional Fixed and Folding Knives with 1095 HC Stainless Steel Blades, Sawcut Bone Handles, and Made in USA for Hunting, Skinning, EDC, Field Dressing, and Outdoor

text_fidelity_a: Saris The Boss Bike Stand, White Most bicycles do not come with built-in kickstands anymore. Even if yours has a kickstand, there are lots of reasons not to use it when you park your bicycle at home or in the office. A kickstand will usually scuff the floor and also makes your bike lean over a lot, thus taking more space. This Saris stand holds the bicycle upright, minimizing the necessary floor space. The smooth bottom to this stand is less likely to scar the floor and you can always put a piece of carpet underneath. Your bike doesn't lean against a wall, either, which can scuff your wall's paint and also scuff your bicycle. The rack holds your bike by the wheel, which is more durable than the carbon fiber used in many frames these days. The rack even folds up and out of the way when not in use. $40 for a nicely made-in-the USA tool is a reasonable price.
text_fidelity_b: Saris The Boss Bike Stand, White
